savings_or_continuation_provisions.quote: Sec. 3. Existing Permits. All permits heretofore issued pursuant to the orders enumerated in section 2(k) of this order, and in force at the date of this order, shall remain in full effect in accordance with their terms unless and until modified, amended, suspended, or revoked by the appropriate authority.
savings_or_continuation_provisions.reaches: permits issued under the revoked orders
savings_or_continuation_provisions.note: Permits issued under EO 13337 and EO 11423 and in force on 2019-04-10 remain in full effect in accordance with their terms; this is the order's savings clause.

transfer_provisions.quote: (b) Except with respect to facilities covered by Executive Order 10485 of September 3, 1953 (Providing for the Performance of Certain Functions Heretofore Performed by the President With Respect to Electric Power and Natural Gas Facilities Located on the Borders of the United States), as amended, and section 5(a) of Executive Order 10530 of May 10, 1954 (Providing for the Performance of Certain Functions Vested in or Subject to the Approval of the President), the Secretary of State is hereby designated to receive all applications for the issuance or amendment of Presidential permits for the construction, connection, operation, or maintenance, at the international boundaries of the United States, of:
transfer_provisions.note: Re-designates the Secretary of State to receive all applications for Presidential permits for cross-border infrastructure, the function EO 11423 sec. 1 gave him.

effective_date_reading: No effective-date wording for sec. 2(k); 'are hereby revoked', so the revocation took effect on signing, 2019-04-10 (printed 84 FR 15492, April 15, 2019). Sec. 2(j)'s May 29, 2020 date is a deadline for State Department regulations, not an effective date.

targets_in_batch_08.EO:11423: sec. 2(k) ('Executive Order 13337 of April 30, 2004 ..., and Executive Order 11423 of August 16, 1968 ..., as amended, are hereby revoked'): whole order, no qualifier; sec. 3 keeps permits already issued in effect.

conclusion: EO 13867 (signed 2019-04-10, 84 FR 15491-15493, read once in full) revises the cross-border Presidential permit process (sec. 2(a)-(j)), revokes EO 13337 and EO 11423, as amended (sec. 2(k)), keeps existing permits in full effect (sec. 3) and has general provisions (sec. 4). The revocation is unqualified and effective on signing; the savings clause protects permits, not provisions of the revoked orders.
